summary: A 1970 note on teletype-style communication between IMPs. It is an early network note about how IMPs themselves might exchange typed text, rather than traffic between hosts.

eli5.summary: This note is about letting the network boxes send typed messages to each other, a bit like text chat between machines.

subtitle: Request to add timestamps to IMP-to-IMP network messages

tldr.problem: When an operator sees a message from another network site on their teletype, they do not know when it was sent, making it hard to decide whether to respond.
tldr.mechanism: This note requests that IMPs add a timestamp to each teletype message they send, using 24-hour time with a time zone designation.
tldr.outcome: A small but useful operational improvement that helped early network administrators manage time-sensitive interactions.

today: This operational note addresses a real problem of early network message handling. Modern message systems include timestamps by default, but in 1970, this was a novel request.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content: An IMP (Interface Message Processor, the early network's routing computers) teletype sometimes receives messages from other sites without timing information. The operator receiving the message does not know if it is fresh or hours old. This is particularly difficult across time zones: many sites span all U.S. time zones and have no direct voice connection, so an operator cannot quickly ask when the message was sent.
sections.eli5: Messages appear on a screen but you don't know when they arrived, which matters for deciding if you should answer.

sections.title: Proposed Solution
sections.content: The RFC requests that every IMP teletype message that causes no response at the receiving end should be tagged with a timestamp. The sending IMP should use 24-hour time and include the time zone designation so the receiving operator knows both what time it was and where that time came from.
sections.eli5: Tag each message with the time it was sent, using a format anyone can understand.

sections.title: Impact
sections.content: This is a straightforward operational improvement for the early network. It is requested that all sites adopt this practice. The note is brief and directed at operators and system administrators of the IMPs rather than specifying a formal protocol change.
sections.eli5: It is a simple idea, but it helps people talking across the network understand each other better.
